translationRepairs: Jing Xiang, styled Zizhen, came from Fenyin in Tongzhou and claimed Tang’s Prince of Pingyang, Hui, as ancestor.
Jing Xiang, styled Zizhen, came from Fengyi in Tongzhou and claimed Tang’s Prince of Pingyang, Hui, as ancestor.
馮翊 is Fengyi, not Fenyin.
Jing Xiang, styled Zizhen, was a native of Fenyin in Tongzhou; he claimed descent from Tang’s Prince of Pingyang, Hui.
Jing Xiang, styled Zizhen, was a native of Fengyi in Tongzhou; he claimed descent from Tang’s Prince of Pingyang, Hui.
馮翊 is Fengyi, not Fenyin.
The army set out toward Guangzhou, was stopped by torrential rain, then besieged Shouzhou without success and lost heavily; only then did Taizu bitterly repent.
The army marched out through Guang Prefecture, was stopped by torrential rain, then besieged Shouzhou without success and lost heavily; only then did Taizu bitterly repent.
光州 is Guang Prefecture, not Guangzhou. Naming it without Guangzhou in parentheses avoids confusion with the southern city.
As a commander Zhen excelled at discipline and choosing men; when Taizu first held Xuanyi, Zhen built his army system, picking officers and drilling troops with real art.
As a commander Zhen excelled at discipline and choosing men; when Taizu first held Xuanwu, Zhen built his army system, picking officers and drilling troops with real art.
The source has 宣武, Xuanwu; Xuanyi is incorrect here.
When Taizu of Liang held Xuannu, he raised five hundred horses into a cavalry force and gave Shigu command; under him Shigu helped break Huang Chao and Qin Zongquan.
When Taizu of Liang held Xuanwu, he raised five hundred horses into a cavalry force and gave Shigu command; under him Shigu helped break Huang Chao and Qin Zongquan.
The source has 宣武, Xuanwu; Xuannu is a typo.

At Luzhou Feng Ba killed the Jin commander Li Kegong and surrendered to Liang. Taizu sent Congzhou in; Jin attacked; Congzhou could not hold and fled to Heyang.
李克恭 is Li Kegong, not Li Keqin.
